svg.text: The two kinds of record day
A page that shares its record day was already being read 30,107 times a day. A page that has it alone was being read 3,947 times a day.
Their record days are the same size: 2,095,287 against 2,092,734.
READERS A DAY BEFORE THE EVENT, ON A LOG SCALE
The bar is the median. 7.6 times apart, Mann-Whitney z -6.704, p under 0.0001, on the 46 and
READERS ON THE RECORD DAY ITSELF
The two medians are 0.1% apart. The record day is the same size either way. What differs is
The page that shared its day multiplied itself 68 times over. The page that had it alone multiplied itself 587 times over.
A record day is either the world turning to a page it already used, or the world finding one it did not know. Only the second kind happens alone.

English Wikipedia daily pageviews, user agents only, Wikimedia REST API. Every article that ever reached the daily top 1,000, 1 July 2015 to 13 August 2026; the 220 largest single reading days on record.

Readers a day before the event is the median of days 21 to 8 before the peak. 6 pages sit under the 20-readers-a-day floor and are drawn at the left edge; they are titles that received their subject's history at the moment of the event, and they are excluded from the test and from the multiples.
Every figure computed from the file by src/lib/findings.js. Nothing typed by hand.
